title: RUNEFORGE 1.2.2 | 100% Procedural | GPT 6 Astra
author: Disastrous-Round-150
selftext:
RUNEFORGE: A 100% Procedural RTS Gets a PvE Conquest Campaign

My Warcraft 3-inspired fantasy RTS has grown into a campaign of expanding settlements, dungeon expeditions, escalating enemies and legendary loot. Here’s what we added across versions 1.2, 1.2.1 and 1.2.2.

The big thing: **100% procedural graphics, music and sound effects.**

Terrain, characters, buildings, surface materials, animation, the UI font and everything you hear are generated in code. Built in C++17/OpenGL with SDL2, without an off-the-shelf game engine or imported art/audio assets.

**v1.2: Seasons of the Deep**

We added a PvE expedition campaign led by Thane and his retinue. Explore the fogged wilderness, enter persistent dungeons, defeat their wardens and recover the seals that unlock the final sanctum.

Loot scales with distance and dungeon difficulty. Procedural weapons, armor and relics progress from Common to Legendary, with bonuses and effects including chain lightning, cleave and lifesteal. Rarity-colored loot beams mark your finds, and equipped gear changes the hero’s glow.

There are surprises along the way: a falling star, a treasure thief, a rescuable stone guardian and treasure chests that might bite back.

**v1.2.1: Conquest of the Deep**

PvE became a full RTS conquest campaign, with gathering, construction, research and army expansion:

• Chop lumber, mine gold and fish for food.  
• Build barracks, lodges, towers, forges and Frontier Halls.  
• Train workers, guards and riflemen, supporting up to 120 population.  
• Expand from the center across a fogged 5 × 5 strategic map.

The wilderness now starts with **630+ enemies and 100 enemy rifts across six outward rings**. Farther rings have more spawn sites, stronger enemies and tougher mixed packs, progressing from restless dead and barrow wights to armored golems, flame wardens and abyssal titans.

Rifts replenish enemies and launch raids. Destroy them, finish their guardians and establish settlements to secure territory permanently.

Your economy and defenses keep running while your expedition is underground. Leaving home undefended has consequences.

Each dungeon now has its own procedural layout and architectural palette:

• Sunken Crypt: moss-green branching catacombs.  
• Frost Cavern: blue ice, irregular chambers and winding passages.  
• Molten Forge: copper-and-basalt industrial halls with lava channels.  
• Ashen Sanctum: violet-and-gold ritual wings around a final arena.

Victory requires all 100 rifts cleared, all 25 sectors held, all four wardens defeated and the ancestral artifact claimed.

**v1.2.2: Seasons of Conquest**

Spring → Summer → Fall → Winter.

Each season lasts four minutes, followed by a one-minute transition. That creates a repeating **20-minute seasonal cycle**, with its exact progress preserved in saves.

Foliage, terrain, lighting, weather and music blend together. Winter adds snow to exposed surfaces and frost-cracked ice to the water.

Across these updates, the procedural renderer gained sculpted SDF geometry, beveled masonry, stone surface detail, ambient occlusion and glowing emissive bloom. The synthesizer gained seasonal arrangements, plucked strings, flute voices, dungeon war drums, cavern reverb, metallic impacts and rarity-specific loot chimes.

You can also hide the entire HUD for a clear view of the world.

The accompanying two-minute **1920 × 1080, 60 fps gameplay showcase** covers all four seasons, increasingly dangerous enemies and all four dungeon wardens, using the game’s own procedural music and sound effects.

Everything you see and hear starts in code.
